questions.question: What is a JSON array?
options: A set of key/value pairs wrapped in { }
An ordered list of values wrapped in [ ]
A reserved JSON keyword meaning 'empty'
An XML-only concept with no JSON equivalent
questions.explanation: An array is an ordered list, written with square brackets — e.g. "tags": ["urgent", "personal"].

questions.question: Why must an Apex wrapper class's field names match the JSON keys to use JSON.deserialize?
options: They don't need to match — Apex guesses the mapping automatically
deserialize maps JSON keys to Apex fields by exact name, so a mismatch leaves the field unpopulated
Apex only supports deserializing into Map, never a custom class
JSON keys are automatically converted to uppercase before matching
questions.explanation: JSON.deserialize matches keys to field names case-sensitively — if the JSON key is userId but the Apex field is userID, it won't populate.

questions.question: What's the difference between JSON.deserialize and JSON.deserializeUntyped?
options: There is no difference, they're aliases
deserialize only works with XML, deserializeUntyped only works with JSON
deserialize maps JSON into a specific Apex class; deserializeUntyped produces generic Map/List structures
deserializeUntyped is faster but less accurate
questions.explanation: deserialize(jsonString, MyClass.class) gives you a typed object; deserializeUntyped gives you generic Map/List structures you cast yourself.

questions.question: In XML, what is a namespace (e.g. declared with xmlns) used for?
options: Encrypting the XML content
Avoiding naming collisions when XML from different sources is combined
Compressing the XML file size
Declaring the XML version number
questions.explanation: Namespaces keep elements like <soap:Envelope> distinct from any other <Envelope> that might appear elsewhere in a combined document.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you assume a JSON field always exists in a real-world API response?
options: JSON doesn't support optional fields at all
APIs often omit a key entirely when it has no value, rather than sending null
Deserialization always fails if any field is missing
Missing fields automatically default to the number 0
questions.explanation: A missing key is different from a null value — check for null (or that the field was populated) after deserializing before relying on it.
